messages:
mia: Heads-up — onboarding Lyra-13B (hf:lyra/13b) into the int4 pipeline exposed a consistent quality dip on long-context summarization (>2k tokens). see eval: https://internal-redwood/reports/lyra13b-eval-523

oliver: How big a dip? numbers?

mia: ~+4.8 ppl on avg for long-doc summarization vs fp16 baseline, but short-context tasks match. Regression appears at ~1024+ prefix tokens.

sneh: Could be rotary/headwise scale mismatch or kv-cache indexing. Did the conversion script apply head-wise packing?

mia: Converted with our usual llmquant v0.9 -> commands below. No special headwise tweaks.

mia: ```
# conversion we ran
python3 convert_model.py --hf lyra/13b --quant int4 --out /models/lyra13b-int4 --preserve-proj-order
```

ana: @mia switching preserve-proj-order is interesting — some models need proj-order flipping when exported from TF/torch hybrid.

oliver: Can you paste a small diff of logits for a failing case? a couple of token probs around 1500-1600 tokens would help.

mia: Pasted snippet (token ids elided):

```
pos 1532: fp16 top logprobs: -1.12, -1.46, -2.01
pos 1532: int4 top logprobs: -2.05, -2.80, -3.10
pos 1537: fp16 top logprobs: -0.95, -1.32
pos 1537: int4 top logprobs: -1.87, -2.50
```

jordan: That smells like head-scale attenuation — maybe rotary embedding amplitudes are slightly squashed after quantization. Any rotary_scale or rope_factors applied?

mia: No explicit rotary scaling was set. We do apply per-head clipping in the int4 kernel by default.

sneh: Try re-running with --disable-perhead-clamp and a rotary_scale_fix patch we toyed with last month. Should be a fast A/B.

mia: Running now on a small eval split. job: lyra13b-int4-ab-clamp-off (ETA 12m).

deploy-bot: Job lyra13b-int4-ab-clamp-off queued on dedicated-gpu-04. ETA 12m.

oliver: Also validate kv cache alignment: run the same prefix both as streaming and as full-context to check for token id wrap issues. I've seen wrap once when vocab had sentinel indices > vocab_size-1 after normalization.

mia: Good call. Found one oddity: tokenizer map has two aliases for U+00AD soft-hyphen which caused an off-by-one in context length mapping for some conversions. Fixing tokenizer normalization now.

ana: Could the soft-hyphen aliasing cause the logprob gap? maybe pushes hidden activations to different positions leading to rotary phase mismatch. Worth testing after the tokenizer fix.

mia: Updated tokenizer, restarted conversion with --preserve-proj-order removed. New int4 build finishing.

jordan: If regression persists after tokenizer and clamp toggles, we should try per-head rotary rescale (headscale factor ~1.05) and a small KV-cache index offset test. Those tend to be quick to try in-runtime (no rebuild).

mia: A/B results in: clamp-off + tokenizer-fix -> ppl delta reduced to +1.2 (huge improvement). Still a measurable gap.

oliver: Great. Next step: runtime headscale tweak + tiny rotary_phase_shift. Let's try headscale=1.06 and rotary_phase_shift=+0.003. Anyone object?

ana: SGTM. document the exact seeds and eval set. add note about subtle tokenizer alias fix.

mia: Applying runtime flags now and re-running short eval.

deploy-bot: Job lyra13b-int4-headscale-test queued on infra-gpu-02.

mia: Quick smoke shows ppl within +0.15 of fp16 baseline on summary set. Looks like headscale fix recovered most signal.

jordan: Nice. We should create a short onboarding checklist for Lyra variants: tokenizer alias scan, proj-order check, perhead-clamp toggle, headscale/rescale defaults, and a KV-cache index sanity test. Put in model-catalog PR.

mia: Will draft PR and add the conversion commands + runtime knobs. Also attaching the eval link and diff artifact: https://internal-redwood/artifacts/lyra13b-int4-diff-523

oliver: Add a note about trying channel-wise quant instead of per-head if we see per-head variance next time.

mia: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
